channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The Lightswitch" - Just a simple lightswitch that turns YOU off and on. Probably.

item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds).

Honestly not sure why you need to go here… its much more interesting of an anomaly without the edgy "they used it to assassinate people" trope.

So the anomaly is interesting, but I feel your execution is fairly tropey. I'd be much more interested in a narrative about identity than about some mystical bad guy from a GOI.

Moreover, there's very little narrative here. As described it is a short concept that is focused on how the anomaly works, without more substantive storytelling.

I think this is a pretty novel idea, and could be used to tell an interesting story, so I would suggest workshopping some concepts that this anomaly could be used to explore.

item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded: Thank you for the feedback! I've made some edits that hopefully help clarify some details, and removed the corpse entirely. I also changed it from having the Bookkeeper be very resilient to struggling to control the many minds within him. I thought about it and realized it would make for a much more interesting interview log!

item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
I like this one, especially because of the binary option, but there are some problems:

1) I'm guessing that if you flick it off it takes your personality, if you flick it on you gain all currently absorbed personalities. This is fine, but you may want to put a limit on that if you have multiple personalities in your head only your personality is absorbed and the others are lost. Otherwise, you could potentially have a ridiculous number of personalities.

2) What are the relative strengths of the personalities? Basically, is there a struggle for control, and what kind of power do the other personalities have regarding the actions of the body? Also, are the personalities relegated to the back and can only watch or do they have any kind of voice in what happens?

3) What happens if you flick it on but it doesn't have a personality? What happens if the personality was already given to someone else? Could you absorb another personality and that personality resurrect the body, albeit under new management?

4) While I like the concept, the corpse personality drain may be one step too far. That's the only thing I would suggest dropping.

5) Strictly as a side note, the multiple personalities may actually make the Bookkeeper easier to threaten. Not only is he the receptacle of multiple lives, and thus making him more willing to make a deal; the more personalities the easier he would be to threaten. Also, the personalities may break and at least debate a deal, meaning that the weakest personality would determine if the person breaks.

But otherwise, great concept!

item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
That one of the best SCPs Ive seen here. I think that when the horror exceeds itself the most, not focusing on the "creature" (or your case the lightswitch) but in the people around it.

What I am thinking is how all the minds inside the librarian collaborate with him? They were a cult? Someone could "escape", leaving notes to the Foundation, or even giving interviews "they are always watching me, the people in my head"

I truly hope you get the greenlight! Have a great day! :D

item.title: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article with most content being in Addendum

Elevator Pitch: A lightswitch that, when flicked on, gives the user life and, when flicked off, takes the user’s life. Things get more interesting when living creatures turn it on and dead creatures turn it off.

Central Narrative: The SCP is simple enough; if you flick it off, it takes your consciousness, rendering you essentially dead/vegetative. If someone forces your corpse/vegetative body to flick it on again, you gain your consciousness back.

Collapsed for mobile users
Collapsed for mobile users

However, if somebody who is alive flicks it on, they absorb the consciousness of the person who flicked it off. This forces two minds to share one body. Although the original host is mostly in control, absorbed consciousness are capable of forcing actions with enough concentration. This will require them to overwhelm the original host, which can be extremely difficult, especially if the host was specifically trained for mental fortitude/self-control. The host can choose to read other consciousnesses' memories, so long as the host can overpower them.

The Foundation recovers the SCP from a GOI (likely MC&D) after someone in the GOI unwittingly flicked it on while alive, causing the user to take the previous user’s consciousness and turn into a human with two minds, with two separate consciousnesses and all of its memories and skills. The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds). The bookkeeper is then interviewed by the Foundation, in which the Foundation attempts to loosen the bookkeeper’s mental strength in order to interview some of the other consciousnesses trapped within. Forcing a corpse/non-organic material to switch it off has no effect.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Keeping it short and simple, with an addendum explaining the GOI’s usage and recovery notes.

Additional Notes: I imagine the article itself will be brief (here is a lightswitch, it turns people on and off, no testing allowed, etc) with an addendum that holds the real meat of the SCP (recovery, interview).

In the interview, the Bookkeeper explains that he is the third iteration of them, and continuously absorbs the previous one before him. He mentions that plans were in place to try and create a sort of “generational immortality”, although they didn’t get very far.
